topics.title: COP31 begins with pressure for practical climate action
topics.summary: Leaders and delegates have gathered in Antalya for COP31, where discussions include climate finance, a fair energy transition, and ways to turn national promises into visible progress.
topics.discussionPrompt: When leaders promise climate progress people can actually notice, what would make the biggest difference around here: cleaner air, cheaper power, better transit, or something else?

topics.title: Ukraine peace talks open in Abu Dhabi
topics.summary: US-led talks involving Ukraine and Russia began in Abu Dhabi, described as the first substantive negotiations in months focused on ending the war and discussing longer-term security.
topics.discussionPrompt: Big negotiations can sound distant. What small sign would make you feel that people were genuinely trying to make everyday life safer and more predictable?

topics.title: Energy permitting bill advances in the US Senate
topics.summary: The US Senate advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding reviews for power projects and infrastructure, as rising electricity demand from data centers reshapes the energy debate.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your neighborhood needed more power, what would you want planners to prioritize first: speed, affordability, clean energy, or a real chance for locals to weigh in?

topics.title: Microsoft raises concerns about data-center component limits
topics.summary: Microsoft has urged US officials to reconsider an expected restriction on new Chinese optical transceivers, saying the move could slow construction of AI data centers.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a crucial gadget part is made far away, does that make technology feel more impressive or more fragile? Which everyday device would be hardest to replace?

topics.title: China flying-car maker targets next-summer launch
topics.summary: A Chinese maker of a two-seat flying-car model says it could begin launches next summer, bringing the long-running futuristic transport idea closer to a public test.
topics.discussionPrompt: If flying cars became normal, would you be first in line, happily watching from the ground, or asking who is going to direct rush-hour traffic in the sky?

topics.title: Australia considers tougher AI incident reporting
topics.summary: Australia released recommendations after an AI-linked breach of a Medicare reporting portal, including consideration of mandatory reporting and penalties for serious regulatory failures.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new technology makes a big mistake, what helps rebuild trust: a quick explanation, an independent check, clearer rules, or simply seeing the fix work?

topics.title: UK youth-platform rules may extend to YouTube Kids
topics.summary: Proposed UK social-media restrictions for under-16s could also cover YouTube Kids, extending the debate over how child-focused platforms should be designed and supervised.
topics.discussionPrompt: What made-for-kids media did you love growing up? If you designed a safer version today, what feature would you keep and what would you change?

topics.title: Drug makers face questions about insulin supply
topics.summary: Experts warn that pharmaceutical companies' focus on popular weight-loss medicines could put pressure on insulin access, especially in places already struggling to obtain diabetes treatment.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a popular new product changes what companies make, how should they balance excitement for the new thing with keeping everyday essentials dependable?

topics.title: Historic ocean liner slated for reef afterlife
topics.summary: Plans are moving ahead to sink a historic ocean liner as a massive artificial reef, giving the retired vessel a proposed new role beneath the waves.
topics.discussionPrompt: Turning an old ship into a reef is quite a second act. What retired building, vehicle, or object would you love to see creatively repurposed?

topics.title: Film crews discuss storyboards in the AI era
topics.summary: Filmmakers are talking about how storyboards help crews share a visual plan, as the industry weighs where newer AI tools can assist without replacing creative collaboration.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather plan a creative project with sketches, a written outline, or just start making it and see where it goes? What usually surprises you most?
